working_title: Pembrokeshire's Golf Courses: A Practical Guide to Playing the Far West of Wales
angle: Pembrokeshire is routinely overlooked by UK golfers chasing Royal Porthcawl or East Lothian, yet it offers a compact cluster of genuine links and coastal courses, from Wales's oldest club at Tenby to the wilder clifftop and estuary layouts further north, all inside a National Park. The post makes a practical case for building a two or three night golf break here, covering the key courses honestly (what they are and aren't), where to stay, and how to get there.
research_notes:
- Tenby Golf Club: established 1888, widely cited as Wales's oldest affiliated golf club. 18-hole links, par 70 (some sources say par 72 after recent reshaping), approx 6,330–6,613 yards depending on source. James Braid extended from 9 to 18 holes in 1907; Donald Steel also credited with later work. Course runs alongside Tenby South Beach, exposed to prevailing south-westerlies. Views over Carmarthen Bay and Caldey Island. Blind shots, pot bunkers, hog's-back fairways, dense gorse. Ranked in Golf Monthly top 100 UK courses (value). Dormy House on-site (11 twin rooms with en-suite). Visitors welcome year-round, handicap required, advance booking needed. High-season visitor fees quoted in one source as approx £85 weekday / £90 weekend (Where2Golf, figures may have moved — do not state as current fact without verification). Ranked 8th best course in Wales by Golf World 2023; 136th best in Britain and Ireland by Golf World 2025. Course noted for excellent natural drainage, playable year-round.
- Newport Links Golf Club (Newport Sands): 18-hole course, par 72, approx 6,112 yards. Situated wholly within Pembrokeshire Coast National Park, between Cardigan and Fishguard, 2-minute drive from the town of Newport. Original 9 holes laid out by James Braid in 1925; extended to 18 in 2008. Front nine is clifftop/elevated; back nine lower, closer to sea, more classically links in character. Preseli Mountains visible on one side, Irish Sea on the other. On-site B&B accommodation (approx 12 twin rooms plus suites). Cat Rock Restaurant/café at clubhouse with views over Newport Bay. Noted by one reviewer as part-links rather than pure links — honest caveat worth including.
- St David's City Golf Club: 11-hole links with 18 tees, par 70, 6,116–6,117 yards. Dry and playable all year. Spectacular views over Ramsey Island, Whitesands Bay and St Davids Head. Located at The Burrows, Whitesands Bay. Good-value, low-key option worth a mention.
- Ashburnham Golf Club (Carmarthenshire, just east of Pembrokeshire border): one of the oldest and most demanding links in Britain, sweeping views of Gower Peninsula. Worth a brief mention as a possible add-on for golfers driving in from the east.
- Pembrokeshire Coast National Park: the whole county sits within or adjacent to it — a genuine draw for non-golfing partners.
- Getting there: Tenby is on the Pembroke Dock rail line from Cardiff (approx 2.5–3 hours). Newport Pembrokeshire is on the A487. Fishguard ferry port (for Ireland) is 15 minutes from Newport Links — could work as a dual-purpose trip.
- Wales has around 180 golf courses in total; Pembrokeshire is rarely the first destination UK visitors name, which is the hook.
- Do NOT fabricate current green fee figures — only Tenby's approx high-season rates appear in research (one source, possibly dated); describe as 'check directly with the club' or omit specifics.
must_avoid: - No invented green fee prices stated as current fact (research figures may be outdated; instruct readers to check directly with clubs). - No fabricated quotes from pros, reviewers, or club staff. - No first-person anecdotes implying the site owner has played these courses. - Do not describe Newport Links as a pure links course — research notes it falls on a spectrum and the front nine is clifftop rather than classic links. - Wales links courses were touched on in the earlier post 'wales-s-links-courses-three-classics-worth-the-drive' — this post must be clearly differentiated by its Pembrokeshire-specific, practical-guide framing and by covering courses (Tenby, Newport, St David's) not featured in that post. - No gambling, betting, health/medical, or financial advice content. - No em dashes anywhere. - UK English throughout (favour, travelling, etc.).
